ety.text: Borrowed from Latin rē, ablative of rēs (“thing, matter, topic”).

chain.g: second degree or note of Guido of Arezzo's hexachordal scales

ety.text: From Glover's solmization, from Middle English re (“second degree or note of Guido of Arezzo's hexachordal scales”), Italian re in the solmization of Guido of Arezzo, from the first syllable of Latin resonāre (“made to resound”) in the lyrics of the scale-ascending hymn Ut queant laxis by Paulus Deacon.

senses.d: About, regarding, with reference to; used especially in letters, documents, emails and case law.
A syllable used in solfège to represent the second note of a major scale.

es:con relación a.gl: regarding; as for; when it comes to

es:con respecto a.gl: with respect to; when it comes to

chain.g: to take up, receive, adopt, accept, or assume

ety.text: From Latin assūmptus. Cognate with English assumption and English assume.

chain.g: to sound or ring again, resound, reecho; call repeatedly

ety.text: From Latin re[sonāre] in the hymn for St. John the Baptist.
